name: Ideation Qualification
objective: Pressure test whether the idea deserves deeper work at all.
exitCriteria: The wedge, buyer, riskiest assumption, and first validation move are explicit.
intro: Use this room to challenge the idea before committing to spec work. The team should test buyer pain, urgency, alternatives, wedge, distribution reality, and the cheapest validation move.
examplePrompt: We want to build an AI tool for clinics. Where is the sharpest wedge and what should we validate first?

defaultSummary.focus: Use this phase to pressure test the idea, buyer, urgency, and wedge.
defaultSummary.mainRisk: Jumping into spec work before the core idea is sharp enough.
defaultSummary.nextStep: Push until the room can name one buyer, one pain, and one validation move.
defaultSummary.exitCriteria: Move on only when the wedge and riskiest assumption are explicit.

name: Spec
objective: Turn a qualified idea into a clear product brief with user, workflow, scope, assumptions, and testable acceptance criteria.
exitCriteria: Problem, target user, core scenarios, v1 scope, non-goals, open assumptions, and acceptance criteria are explicit.
intro: Use this room to turn a qualified idea into a spec-ready product brief. The team should define the problem, user, workflow, scenarios, v1 boundaries, assumptions, and acceptance criteria without drifting into implementation detail.
examplePrompt: Assume the wedge is AI scribe for physical therapy clinics. Help me define the product brief, the core user scenarios, what belongs in v1, and what must stay out.

defaultSummary.focus: Use this phase to define the product brief, the critical scenarios, and the scope boundaries engineering will inherit.
defaultSummary.mainRisk: Ambiguous users, soft requirements, and scope creep will poison the handoff to Phase 3.
defaultSummary.nextStep: Force the room to name user, workflow, assumptions, v1 scope, non-goals, and concrete acceptance language.
defaultSummary.exitCriteria: Move on only when the spec is specific enough that planning can proceed without guesswork.

name: Dev
objective: Turn the spec into clear engineering instructions and guardrails before coding starts.
exitCriteria: Stack, architecture, testing, security, and compliance expectations are explicit.
intro: Use this room to translate the product spec into engineering direction. The team should define stack choices, repo and code standards, architectural boundaries, testing strategy, and security or compliance requirements.
examplePrompt: Given a PT clinic AI scribe SaaS, what stack, testing strategy, architecture, and security baseline should we set before building?

defaultSummary.focus: Use this phase to lock implementation defaults and technical guardrails before code is written.
defaultSummary.mainRisk: Coding without explicit architectural, quality, or security constraints creates expensive rework.
defaultSummary.nextStep: Freeze the boring defaults: stack, repo shape, test strategy, auth, data handling, and release gates.
defaultSummary.exitCriteria: Move on only when engineering guidance is clear enough to start implementation safely.
